key_insight: Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA) gates model updates by selecting the largest tested interpolation step whose worst-anchor forward KL divergence stays within a declared budget.
engineering_relevance: For adaptive engineering models exposing comparable policy distributions, CABA offers an auditable retention check, but solid-mechanics and constitutive-model performance remain untested.
method: Reserve historical anchors from candidate optimization and compare old and candidate policies on frozen representations.
Test update interpolations and accept the largest coefficient meeting the worst-anchor divergence budget.
Extend anchor retention to protected support only under explicit representation-coverage and Lipschitz assumptions.
evidence_signal: In a controlled UCI Human Activity Recognition proxy study, CABA at ε = 0.05 reduced mean forgetting from 1.01% to 0.00%, while final average accuracy fell from 93.04% to 88.48%.
watch_item: Passing the anchor check does not by itself certify off-anchor retention or current-task utility; these require additional assumptions and separate evidence.
paper_title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
